title: Recent grad treated in Richland after breaking his neck in Columbia River - NewsBreak
text:
By Annette Cary ,
15 hours ago Noah Barnsley, 18, broke his neck when he jumped into the Columbia River at Vantage. A friend saved him from drowning. GoFundMe A recent graduate of Ellensburg High is being treated in Richland after breaking his neck jumping into the Columbia River at Vantage on Thursday.
Noah Barnsley, 18, now faces “an unimaginable challenge,” says a GoFundMe to help pay for his medical expenses, travel between hospitals and the needs of his family as they support and care for him.
His friends were with him at the river, and one of them, Jake Snow, jumped into the water and saved him from drowning, Noah’s mother, Laine Barnsley, posted on Facebook .
Her son regained consciousness as Snow did CPR, but was unable to move his body, his mother said.
Noah was flown by air ambulance to Kadlec Regional Medical Center in Richland , where he underwent surgery Friday. He had two shattered vertabrae removed, and a cage was used to stabilize other broken vertebrae.
Another surgery is planned to stabilize his neck on Thursday.
“Things change by the minute, but he is talking and cracking jokes,” his mother posted. Having his friends visiting at the hospital has been the best medicine, she said.
When Noah heard a fundraiser had been started, his mother posted that “he said, in typical Noah fashion — Sweet, for my truck?”
But he also has had emotional ups and downs as medical staff have not been able to predict how much mobility he will regain.
Noah’s mother posted on Monday that he was able to stretch his left arm out and then try to scratch his head. On Tuesday, she posted that he was able to control his trunk.
“The feeling in his arms is constantly changing which means things are happening and waking up!” his mom posted. “He is getting more sensation in his right leg.”
She considers the family “unbelievably blessed” just by the fact that he is alive and breathing.
“It is truly a miracle, and we’ve been reminded by staff,” she said.
The family has been overwhelmed with the outpouring of support and help they have received, starting shortly after Noah’s accident. They were already known for giving generously to the Ellensburg community, the GoFundMe said.
Noah Barnsley, 18, is shown with his family. The recent Ellensburg High graduate was flown by air ambulance to Kadlec hospital in Richland after breaking his neck during a jump into the Columbia River at Vantage. GoFundMe “Throughout this ordeal, Laine and Jeff are doing everything they can to care for Noah and their two other children, all while navigating the emotional and logistical hurdles that come with such sudden crisis,” the GoFundMe said.
Noah’s father, Jeff Barnsley, serves with the Kittitas County Sheriff’s Office and deputies who responded to the river gave him constant updates on his son.
The air ambulance pilot who flew Noah to Kadlec called Noah’s father after the hospital drop off to tell him his son was stable and urge him not to speed during the drive to the hospital.
Noah’s mother, a teacher, was four hours out-of town with no car, but friends and family joined together to get her to the hospital, she posted online.
Plans are that after Noah heals some he will travel by ambulance to St. Luke’s Rehabilitation Medical Center in Spokane for a 21-day intensive spinal program. His mother will stay in Spokane for those three weeks.
He may return for another surgery in Richland but then will be working to transition to St. Luke’s outpatient care, and one of his parents will be staying with him in Spokane.
